html:
LoMa (Nordström, Edstedt et al. 2026): sparse matching of two photos of one scene: DaD keypoints, DeDoDe-G descriptions (VGG19 plus DINOv2) and a light LightGlue-style transformer matcher; matches as keypoint index pairs (the form COLMAP takes). MIT code and weights; DINOv2 Apache-2.0.

Commercial use: yes.

Details
  • Original code: https://github.com/davnords/loma at ecc947d44ddc
  • Code licence: MIT AND Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: LICENSE, LICENSE-DAD, LICENSE-DEDODE, LICENSE-DINOv2
  • Weights licence: MIT AND Apache-2.0 (assumed from code)
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/davnords/loma/blob/ecc947d44ddc9d50387e887bbedc743d65ffac00/README.md#license ; https://github.com/Parskatt/dad/blob/41b9e86a1a3ae52128485cc1094aa4952ef489ba/LICENSE ; https://github.com/Parskatt/DeDoDe/blob/6d156183f4dc84cd704ae779eebc8350995c5b06/README.md#license
  • Training data: MegaDepth (Internet photo collections with SfM / MVS depth) (Matcher: MegaDepth (paper); DaD: MegaDepth-based distillation (DaD paper); DeDoDe-G descriptor: MegaDepth; B, L, G and R include frozen DINOv2 (LVD-142M). B64 and B128 use VGG descriptors.)
  • Options: max_keypoints = 2048 (>= 1), long_side = 1024 (>= 16), size = 784 (>= 56)
  • Kernel libraries: loma_descriptor, igev, cutlass_conv, cudnn_hacc
  • Variants: loma-b, loma-b64, loma-b128, loma-l, loma-g, loma-r
  • Public TensorRT export is unavailable for loma-b (the bundled BF16 build reduces relative pose AUC@5 by 9.87 points on 50 MegaDepth pairs; use ONNX export and a separate engine build).
  • Outputs: keypoints1, keypoints2, pairs, scores
  • Input size: any H x W >= 32, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): loma-b 3000x4000 (2.4 GiB peak allocated, 3.6 reserved); loma-b64 3000x4000 (1.1 GiB peak allocated, 1.4 reserved); loma-b128 3000x4000 (1.1 GiB peak allocated, 1.4 reserved); loma-l 3000x4000 (2.1 GiB peak allocated, 2.8 reserved); loma-g 3000x4000 (2.6 GiB peak allocated, 3.3 reserved); loma-r 3000x4000 (2.0 GiB peak allocated, 2.7 reserved)
  • loma-b 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 143 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT bf16 176 s (ONNX + engine).
  • loma-b64 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 87 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT bf16 102 s (ONNX + engine).
  • loma-b128 768x1024, first call: portable + torch.compile 86 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT bf16 103 s (ONNX + engine).

  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults). OpenCV essential-matrix RANSAC (0.5 px threshold, normalised by the mean focal length); AUC of the larger of the rotation and translation-direction errors. Both modes receive pairs resized to 768 x 1024. Map matched pixels to the calibrated evaluation coordinates and use the same RANSAC seed per pair. The same 300 pairs for all modes, so float32 and bfloat16 compare pair for pair. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.011 vs the original. GPU, portable bfloat16 and kernels float16 (the defaults): mean |diff| <= 0.05 and p99 <= 0.6 (absolute error of the output keypoints1).

Limitations

  • The standalone B and L BF16 TensorRT engines at 768 x 1024 were compared on ten shifted photos. Minimum match precision within 2 px was 96.62% for B and 95.46% for L.
  • For LoMa-B at 768 x 1024 BF16, export ONNX and build TensorRT in a fresh process. On the first 50 calibrated MegaDepth pairs, AUC@5 was 64.16 portable, 62.97 with the separately built plan, and 54.30 with the bundled TensorRT export.
  • Sparse output: no dense warp. result.matches() gives the matched points for estimate_pose; pairs are the index pairs pycolmap / COLMAP databases take.
  • One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
  • The match count depends on the image pair. The fixed 768 x 1024 LoMa-B64 TensorRT export returns variable-length matches. On ten photos paired with shifted copies, at least 96.7% of TensorRT correspondences agreed with portable within 2 pixels in both images.
  • Two resizes per image as upstream: the detector sees a long side of long_side (aspect kept), the descriptor a size x size square whatever the aspect ratio.
  • LoMa-R uses rotation augmentation. The other variants are trained for upright images.
